A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Renamed components and relocated analyses can be matched reliably despite the substantial revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-classification experiments on PACS, DomainNet, CIFAR-10-W, and CCT, together with ensemble, scaling, and prompt-diversity analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original classification and multimodal reasoning experiments, component ablations, and appendix results for joint training and data selection.

M1.justification: v2's two-stage prompt rewriting becomes HIRPG, which recurrently uses previous prompts as negative examples within a hierarchy. Generator-average weighting in DISCOBER becomes truncated, normalized sample-level sampling in CONAN. v3 also introduces LLM selection of hard-negative concepts for multimodal learning (Sections 4.1–4.3 and A.4). These change the procedure beyond renaming.

E1.justification: v3 adds Bongard-HOI and Bongard-OpenWorld evaluations involving concept answering and classification relative to positive/negative support sets. CCT coverage is removed; PACS, DomainNet, and CIFAR-10-W remain. NICO is named in v3, but corresponding settings and results are not identifiable, so its actual use is unclear.

E2.justification: v3 adds synthetic-data/prompt comparators including Glide-Syn, LE, CHB, SC, and CCG; established coreset selectors including CRAIG, GradMatch, and LCMat; and training-free classifiers in joint training. The CIFAR-10-W continual comparison drops MA (Table 13), although MA participates in the new joint-training comparison.

E3.justification: Reported DomainNet batch size changes from 64 to 128 and memory from 8,000 to 10,000; CIFAR-10-W memory increases from 1,000 to 2,000. v3 uses ER throughout, replaces Gemini with a reported GPT-4/GPT-4o setup, and changes the generator pool from four to five models, replacing DALL.E-2 with SD3 and AuraFlow. New protocols include LLaVA fine-tuning, CIDEr evaluation, and 10-epoch joint training.

E4.justification: v3 adds separate HIRPG/CONAN controls, an RPG-versus-hierarchical-RPG ablation, recognizability/diversity comparisons, and comparative prompt case studies. Earlier web-data ensemble tests, CCT scaling, Gemini-versus-GPT-3.5 analysis, and LPIPS/DISTS analyses disappear. PACS scaling and RMD/Rarity examples are retained and relocated, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both retain five random seeds and mean/SEM reporting for continual-learning results. v3 explicitly associates the seeds with five randomized task splits, while its new joint-training Tables 9–10 report point estimates without uncertainty despite the general SEM statement. No increase in run count is established.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced or added. For example, proposed-method PACS OOD AAUC with ER/ResNet-18 is 35.69 in v2 Table 3 and 38.53 in v3 Table 4, under revised prompt/generator settings rather than a controlled same-setting comparison. v3 adds Bongard, joint-training, and extensive comparator results, while removing CCT results.

T1.justification: v3 introduces formal recurrences for RPG/HIRPG (Equations 1–2) and revises the selection-probability definition from generator-level to normalized sample-level weighting. The RMD definition and incremental mean/covariance derivations remain substantially unchanged in Appendix A.20. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the claimed applicability from continual image classification to multimodal visual reasoning. They introduce a distinct contribution claim for HIRPG and emphasize efficient coreset selection through CONAN. The overarching claim that generated data can outperform web-scraped and manually annotated alternatives is retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving long-context failures, hierarchical prompting, hard-negative generation, and the limits of large-scale pretraining for OOD generalization. It also acknowledges that HIRPG does not compare prompts across branches. Earlier CCT failure explanations and web-data ensemble interpretations disappear; limitations concerning learner feedback and domain-specific generation remain in A.27.

D1.justification: v3 adds optimizer and learning-rate specifications, GPU information, temperature/truncation settings, hierarchy parameters, multimodal input prompts, and five pseudocode algorithms. Dataset access instructions change, and a code/data-split release commitment is added. These substantially expand documentation, although A.3's GPT-4 specification conflicts with GPT-4o in A.10.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially redirected toward coreset selection and synthetic-data prompt generation. New connections to contrastive in-context learning, long-context limitations, and generative replay sharpen distinctions from prior approaches (v3 Sections 2 and A.18). This exceeds bibliographic updates or relocation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. v3 adds a standalone problem statement and reorganizes the appendix into A.1–A.27, moving scaling, RMD justification, and limitations out of the main text. Framework terminology, author information, and document headers also change.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the framework diagram, adds Bongard task illustrations and extensive data-acquisition image grids, and restructures comparison and ablation tables. Earlier prompt-diversity and CCT displays are removed, while retained RMD examples and PACS scaling are relocated. The document also adopts a substantially different template and layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the method's distinct contributions: v2 mainly compares data sources across continual learners, whereas v3 directly evaluates competing prompt-generation and coreset methods and adds independent component controls (Tables 1, 3–5, 11, and 18). Multimodal evaluations and fuller implementation documentation further improve assessment of the approach. Removing CCT and multi-learner coverage reduces breadth, and GPT-4/GPT-4o and repeated DomainNet-value inconsistencies weaken reproducibility. Nevertheless, the stronger method-specific comparisons and ablations provide a substantial net quality gain.
